blockMcqs.question: What is the near-universal first step in interval problems?
options: Build a hash set of all endpoints
Sort the intervals, usually by start
Compare every pair of intervals
Convert each interval to a graph edge
blockMcqs.explanation: Sorting groups related intervals adjacently so one linear pass solves the problem.

blockMcqs.question: After sorting by start so a ≤ c, when do [a,b] and [c,d] overlap?
options: When a ≤ d
When b ≤ c
When c ≤ b
When d ≤ a
blockMcqs.explanation: With starts ordered, the only remaining condition is the second starting before the first ends.

blockMcqs.question: Why must merging use max(current.end, next.end) instead of next.end?
options: To keep the result sorted by end
A nested shorter interval would shrink the merge
To handle negative endpoints correctly
max is faster than assignment
blockMcqs.explanation: A later interval like [2,3] inside [1,10] is shorter; plain assignment would corrupt the end.

blockMcqs.question: In a sweep line, what does the running counter represent?
options: The total number of intervals seen
Intervals overlapping at the current moment
The remaining intervals to process
The index of the current event
blockMcqs.explanation: Each +1 adds an active interval and each −1 removes one, so the count is current overlap.

blockMcqs.question: At equal times, why process the −1 end before the +1 start?
options: To keep the event array stable-sorted
So a room frees up before the next meeting claims it
Because subtraction is cheaper than addition
To avoid integer overflow in the counter
blockMcqs.explanation: Ending first means touching intervals don't both count, matching half-open semantics.

blockMcqs.question: Intersecting two sorted lists, which interval do you advance past?
options: The one that starts earliest
The one with the larger span
The one that ends first
Always the list-A interval
blockMcqs.explanation: The earlier-ending interval cannot overlap anything later, so it is safe to drop.

blockMcqs.question: Which problem requires sorting by end rather than start?
options: Merging overlapping intervals
Inserting one interval into a sorted list
Maximizing non-overlapping intervals kept
Finding peak concurrent overlap
blockMcqs.explanation: Greedy activity selection frees the resource earliest by keeping the soonest-ending interval.

blockMcqs.question: Why is comparing all interval pairs a poor approach?
options: It needs the input pre-sorted anyway
It is O(n²) and times out on large inputs
It cannot detect touching endpoints
It uses O(n²) extra memory
blockMcqs.explanation: Sort-then-sweep is O(n log n); pairwise checking blows up past 10⁵ intervals.
